raw_response.printed_headline_estimate: Section 4.3.1-4.3.3 (PDF pp. 11-12; 2009 baseline N=220, 2019 end-line N=415 [n=220 treatment, n=195 control]): treatment vs. control Veolia piped-water collection p = 2.2 x 10^-16 and adult sanitary latrine use p = 0.0051 (contrasts/SEs not printed); baseline vs. end-line Veolia acceptance p ~ 2.2 x 10^-16, daily drinking and cooking water demand 95% CIs (2.285, 20.71) and (4.785, 34.57) (p ~ 2.2 x 10^-16), sanitary latrine access 11% to 96% (p ~ 0.002); end-line omnibus ANOVAs (no F/beta/SE printed): income & family size on safe-water affordability p = 2.441 x 10^-7, preference for internal house connection p = 0.0004057 (income x literacy x DTW ownership interaction p = 0.02215), household DTW asset ownership on Veolia adoption p = 0.0053, income on WTP p = 0.2215, water quality x purification on diarrhea p = 0.00057.
raw_response.publication_year_note: Published 12 July 2024 in Water, Vol. 16, Issue 14, Article 1978 (Received: 22 May 2024; Revised: 4 July 2024; Accepted: 10 July 2024; Copyright 2024).
raw_response.rationale: The paper reports inferential hypothesis tests (paired/independent tests and omnibus ANOVAs on household survey data from Goalmari, Bangladesh: 2009 baseline N=220 and 2019 end-line N=415 with n=220 treatment and n=195 control), along with exploratory PCA/clustering and deterministic Netica Bayesian Network scenario propagations. However, none of the inferential tests evaluate a narrow rule-type legal, tenure, tariff, administrative, or utility-ownership exposure on a service-access outcome: (1) the baseline-vs-endline and treatment-vs-control tests of collecting Veolia piped water (p = 2.2 x 10^-16) compare generic physical piped-network project presence vs. pre-intervention/unserved control villages (failing narrow Criterion 2, and omitting point contrasts/SEs); (2) the end-line ANOVAs test socio-demographic and household-endowment predictors—income, family size, literacy, and private household ownership of an existing deep tube well asset—on perceived affordability, willingness to pay, preference for an internal connection, Veolia adoption, or diarrhea prevalence (failing Criterion 2 and/or Criterion 4, with only omnibus p-values printed); and (3) the tariff/operational-rule mechanism of interest (the 5,000 BDT advance house-connection fee and Veolia shutting down 6 of 24 community tap standpoints for cost recovery, plus public vs. collective vs. private DTW cost-sharing) is presented only as descriptive counts/narrative (PDF p. 9) and non-inferential Bayesian Network forward/backward probability simulations without uncertainty estimates or hypothesis tests (Tables 2-3, PDF pp. 17-20).
